# CSF shared vocabulary

Source: [architecture.csf](architecture.csf). This dictionary defines the names used in generated diagrams.
It describes a documentation model; it does not verify controller execution or deployed behavior.

| Identifier | Name | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| `observe` | Observe | Read the available measurements, logs and outputs from an execution. |
| `retrieve` | Retrieve | Find relevant saved sources, earlier results and relationships. |
| `choose` | Choose | Select a proposed action or candidate controller from the allowed choices. |
| `check` | Check | Apply the configured contract, bounds and admission rules before execution. Passing these checks does not establish physical safety. |
| `execute` | Execute | Run an admitted action in its configured environment. |
| `evaluate` | Evaluate | Compare the result with criteria chosen independently of the candidate being evaluated. |
| `save_evidence` | Save evidence | Keep the candidate, observed result and source references so the result can be inspected and reused. This was previously called retain; it does not mean retrain. |
| `improve` | Improve | Use evaluated results to select a better controller or revise an allowed workflow. The complete autonomous learning loop is planned. |
| `select_controller` | Select a controller between episodes | The existing bounded CPU search compares candidate results and keeps or rejects controllers between episodes. Connecting this selection to an autonomous agent's next decision remains planned. |
| `retrain` | Retrain | Update a model's learned parameters using training data. This is one possible improvement method, not a required step of every iteration. |
| `human` | Human or agent client | The caller that supplies a task and policy and uses CSF's exposed operations. |
| `brain` | Models and agents | The consumer's reasoning and training components that propose actions. A language model's proposal is not permission to execute it. |
| `agent` | Agent | A named worker definition with versioned instructions, assigned tasks and linked execution records. The current example prepares this definition; there is no shared registry yet. |
| `assignment` | Assignment | One task given to an agent definition, with its own identifier and ticket reference. |
| `checkpoint` | Task checkpoint | A saved typed task record containing its owner, status, next action, evidence and preceding checkpoint identifier, so another agent can resume the work. |
| `work_continuity` | Work continuity | The task checkpoint library at candace/pkg/workcontinuity. It reads, validates and records checkpoints against a caller-supplied issue source. It owns no background workers or service lifetime; the Workbench calls it within the existing CSF runtime. |
| `session` | Workbench conversation session | A conversation and its execution records under a stable identifier. CSF stores Workbench sessions; the current Copilot backend still manages its working context. This is distinct from a gotth-live UI connection. |
| `ui_session` | Live UI session | One accepted gotth-live WebSocket connection and the server-side state maintained for that connection. Each connection initializes its own widget state values; a reconnect creates a new session. Separate values can still refer to shared mutable objects. This is not a stored agent conversation or a memory-isolation boundary. |
| `context` | Context | The information supplied to a model for a particular decision. CSF-owned snapshots and compression remain planned. |
| `contracts` | Shared typed contracts | Protobuf messages, Liquid Proto predicates and OpenAPI operations that define data shapes and allowed calls. Their generators produce bindings and transport code. |
| `application` | Application | Reserved for a runnable composition whose execution owns a process and runtime. A widget, service, page or web layer mounted inside that process is not another application. |
| `runtime` | Runtime | For CSF deployment and runtime counts, the application execution hosted by one process. Mounting a service or widget does not add a runtime; goroutines and OS threads are separate units. |
| `widget` | Widget | A component of gotth-live that presents typed state and accepts events. Widgets exist within gotth-live; they are not independent components mounted directly into an application. A widget does not own a process or runtime. |
| `gotth_live` | gotth-live | The required owner of widgets and their web interaction. It belongs to CSF's web layer and runs within the application's existing process/runtime. |
| `app` | App | A runnable composition of services. Launching an app instance creates an application process; a Go app has its own Go runtime. Mounting another service inside that app does not create another process or runtime. The app owns the root lifetime. |
| `process` | CSF: one Go application process | One running application with a shared address space. Its host owns listeners, startup, shutdown and any configured worker goroutines. |
| `service` | Service | The required lifecycle contract for an SDK capability mounted into the caller's process. A service may share its host's lifetime without another scope, goroutine or process, or declare a shorter child lifetime. Each service performs its own cleanup: release its resources, stop and join its goroutines, and report failures. Its host triggers shutdown and waits for it; the host does not reimplement the child's cleanup. Borrowed resources keep their declared owner. Common enforcement and migration are pending. |
| `http_service` | HTTP service | In the proposed recursive lifecycle contract, a service that manages an HTTP server and mounted child services. It participates in its parent's startup and shutdown, performs its own server cleanup, and asks its children to perform theirs. The application main function owns the root service's lifetime. Registering routes alone does not implement this contract. |
| `live_ui_service` | gotth-live service | The in-process capability that manages live UI connections and their goroutines for a host app. Its lifetime can span many shorter connections. The current Go type is live.App; it does not require another application process. Its bounded effect drain does not yet guarantee every effect has stopped at teardown. |
| `database_io` | Database I/O capability | Planned optional database access for a service. Construction, configuration and mounting do not create a pool, acquire a connection or ping the database. The first operation that needs storage initializes a service-owned pool or uses a borrowed pool. The service closes only pools it created, after dependent work has completed; borrowed pools retain their caller's owner. A pool can manage many connections and is not itself a connection. |
| `mount` | Mount | In the proposed ginService.Mount(child) API, attach a child service to the parent's lifecycle: startup, shutdown signaling and waiting for the child to finish its own cleanup. Existing Register(router) only registers HTTP routes and does not supply these guarantees. |
| `manager` | Manager | Policy that selects or coordinates services when that decision is dynamic. The name does not create a process or a separate lifetime. |
| `scope` | Scope | An explicit lifetime with one owner, cancellation and completion. Cancellation requests shutdown; joining waits until children have exited. |
| `ownership_transfer` | Ownership transfer | An explicit API agreement that hands responsibility for a specified mutable payload from sender to receiver. After a successful handoff, the sender stops accessing it through retained aliases until ownership is returned. Go channel sends copy values and do not invalidate pointers or deep-copy referenced data. Borrowed dependencies keep their owners; cancellation and submission acknowledgement do not establish completion or return of ownership. |
| `process_boundary` | Process boundary | A crossing into another address space. The target is one audited subprocess gateway owning launch, input/output, cancellation, waiting and cleanup; consolidation is pending. Remote protocols retain their own named adapters. |
| `goroutine` | Goroutine | A Go function executing concurrently inside its application's process. It shares memory with other goroutines; its owner must arrange cancellation and completion. |
| `thread` | OS thread | An execution context scheduled by the operating system. Go schedules runnable goroutines onto OS threads; a package name does not assign either one to a CPU core. |
| `core` | CPU core | A hardware execution resource on which the operating system schedules threads. Placement and latency require observation or explicit configuration. |
| `bench` | Workbench | The user entry point for sessions, tools and inspection. Chat, inspection and keyed Kanban widgets exist; further widget composition remains planned. |
| `api` | Generated HTTP, CLI and MCP operations | The generated ways to invoke the same CSF operation contracts. Go callers can also compose libraries directly. |
| `transport_adapter` | HTTP/MCP adapter | The CSF Service registers generated HTTP routes with the caller's Gin router and exposes MCP handlers. It owns no listener, process or independent service lifetime. |
| `mcp` | MCP | Model Context Protocol: the tool-discovery and invocation protocol used by agent clients. Registration does not start another service inside an already running CSF host. |
| `knowledge` | Knowledge and retrieval | Saved documents, source references and explicit relationships exposed through search and graph operations. Coverage depends on what was actually ingested. |
| `symbolic` | Symbolic relationship | An explicit named connection between identified records, such as a source and an artifact derived from it. It is distinct from similarity in an embedding search. |
| `compiler` | Bounded controller compiler | The implemented translation of a restricted controller expression into instructions. The Lean theorem covers its mathematical model; native implementations have separate checks. |
| `compile` | Compile | Translate a source representation into another representation while checking its declared rules. Each compiler names its input, output and guarantees; translating documentation does not prove a robot controller. |
| `workers` | Configured worker goroutines | Concurrent workers in the shared Go process that submit, inspect and cancel configured simulation jobs. Current durable job dispatch uses PostgreSQL; memory-first dispatch remains planned. |
| `inspect` | Inspection | Operations that expose available usage, duration, job state and saved receipts. Missing data is reported as missing, not measured zero. |
| `stores` | PostgreSQL and artifact storage | Configured persistence for records and original artifact bytes. OpenSearch provides searchable document and log views of those sources. |
| `opensearch` | OpenSearch | The configured search and aggregated-log system. Saved source records can also be used to reconstruct trace observations. |
| `jobs` | Simulator and AWS Batch adapters | Code for configured external CARLA, Isaac Sim or AWS Batch execution. Local simulator examples have evidence; real AWS execution still needs configuration and acceptance. |
| `views` | Prometheus, Grafana and Langfuse | Configured systems for measurements, dashboards and agent traces. They display available observations; their existence does not imply every operation was traced. |
| `experiments` | Training results and optional MLflow | Saved experiment artifacts and evaluation results, optionally associated with an MLflow run. Bounded CPU controller search exists; autonomous neural training is not demonstrated. |
| `vendor` | Consumer Copilot backend | The existing model access and file/tool execution loop supplied by Copilot. Future CSF context ownership must use supported backend capabilities. |
| `web` | Web layer | HTTP routing, typed APIs, browser connections, event delivery, server rendering and browser updates in the shared host. Workbench uses this layer; widget interaction belongs to gotth-live within it. |
| `widgets` | Widget SDK and gotth-live | The SDK defines typed widgets within gotth-live. The Workbench Kanban uses gotth-live-owned card instances in the shared host; live WDL installation remains planned. Widgets share host memory, without private heaps or a required goroutine per widget. Shared mutable state needs explicit ownership and synchronization. Bounded effect draining does not guarantee complete joining before teardown. |
| `spine` | Consumer C++ control loop | The proposed fast controller outside slow model reasoning. Integration needs consumer-specific timing, switching and cleanup rules and has not been demonstrated here. |
| `hardware` | Consumer sensors and actuators | Physical devices, potentially reached through CAN or other adapters. Simulator success does not establish safe physical operation. |
| `engine` | Engine | Not a CSF lifecycle category. Gin Engine and Docker Engine keep their upstream meanings. Curiosity Engine is a tentative product name for the planned improvement loop, not an implemented runtime component. |
| `source_recipe` | Agent definition and assignment file | The typed agent.json input to the example, naming the worker, task, ticket, model and repository. |
| `prepare` | PrepareAgentAssignment | The generated HTTP/MCP operation and pure Go preparation function that validate a recipe and calculate stable assignment identities without submitting work. |
| `plan` | Prepared assignment | An immutable recipe snapshot with content hashes and retry identities. Preparation does not create a session or establish task success. |
| `requests` | Generated Workbench requests | Existing generated session and prompt request types populated from the prepared assignment. |
| `worktree` | Session and worktree records | The existing Workbench conversation and isolated repository checkout associated with the submitted assignment. |
| `receipt` | Assignment receipt | The returned links among agent, ticket, session, turn and worktree. A turn identifier acknowledges prompt acceptance; it does not prove completion. |
| `local_job` | Simulator container | A configured local CARLA or Isaac container outside the CSF process. Its output bytes stay in the configured artifact volume. |
| `submit` | SubmitSimulation | Admit a bounded request and record a simulation job for a configured worker. |
| `admitted` | Recorded simulation job | The persisted identity, requested configuration and current state of an admitted job. |
| `start_job` | Start configured local profile | The worker asks the external container platform to start the selected simulator configuration. |
| `poll_job` | Read simulator status, progress and logs | The existing worker observes its configured job and records available simulation steps and output references. |
| `observations` | Saved simulation observations | Persisted job state, measurements, log records and references to original output artifacts. |
| `inspect_job` | InspectSimulation | Read a simulation job's retained state, measurements and artifact references through the generated operation. |
